Furthermore, video games are increasingly being recognized for their therapeutic benefits, moving beyond their reputation as mere forms of entertainment. In fact, research by McGonigal (2012) suggests that games like "SuperBetter," which incorporate psychological concepts, can have a profound impact on mental health. Not only can they help alleviate symptoms of anxiety and depression, but they can also aid in the recovery process from physical trauma. Moreover, these games tap into the potential of positive psychology, leveraging the power of video games to inspire and engage players in their own healing process. Additionally, by incorporating elements of cognitive-behavioral therapy and social support, these games can provide a unique and effective way to promote mental well-being. And, as the field continues to evolve, it's likely that we'll see even more innovative uses of video games in the pursuit of mental health and wellness.
